Convert an htna network to an igraph graph

Source: R/as_igraph_htna.R
as.igraph.htna.Rd

as.igraph() converts a heterogeneous transition network to an 'igraph' graph and keeps its actor partition. Many network measures and algorithms are available for 'igraph' graphs; because the partition is kept, a measure computed in 'igraph' can still be summarized by actor type, for example to compare the centrality of human and AI codes.

as.igraph() creates a weighted graph from the transition weights, stores the actor type of every vertex as the vertex attribute actor_type, the ordered actor types as the graph attribute actor_levels and the estimation method as htna_method. A grouped network is converted cohort by cohort; each graph also records its cohort name in the graph attribute cohort. It returns an igraph graph, or a list of graphs, one per cohort, for a grouped network.

For the edge and node tables of the network without 'igraph', use as.data.frame.htna().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'htna'
as.igraph(x, mode = NULL, weighted = TRUE, diag = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'htna_group'
as.igraph(x, mode = NULL, weighted = TRUE, diag = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

x

An htna network from build_htna() or an htna_group.

mode

Graph mode. Default NULL: "directed" for a directed network, "undirected" otherwise.

weighted

Use the transition weights as edge weights. Default TRUE.

diag

Keep self-transitions as loops. Default TRUE.

...

Further arguments to igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix().

Value

An igraph graph for an htna network. For an htna_group, a named list of igraph graphs, one per cohort, of class c("htna_igraph_group", "list").

Conditions

htna_bad_input when x is not an htna network or an argument is invalid; htna_unassigned_node when a node has no actor type.

See also

build_htna(), as.data.frame.htna(), centralities_htna()

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
graph <- igraph::as.igraph(net)
igraph::vertex_attr(graph, "actor_type")
#>  [1] "AI"    "Human" "AI"    "AI"    "Human" "Human" "AI"    "Human" "AI"   
#> [10] "AI"    "Human" "Human"
